05. 1.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/ Physical Mode).
2.
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner-Appellant as well as learned counsel for the Respondent-State.
3. The present I.A. has been filed with a prayer to release the Petitioner-Appellant on interim bail on the ground of illness of his mother.

4. Learned counsel for the Petitioner-Appellant, at the outset, contended that the Appellant has been convicted by judgment dated 24.08.2024 in a Special Case No.256 of 2018 which corresponds to Trial No.85 of 2022 by the learned Additional District and Sessions Judge-cum-Special Court under POCSO Act, Balasore for commission of an offence punishable under Sections 366/376/323 of IPC read with Section 6 of POCSO Act.

Accordingly, the appellant has been convicted and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/- (rupees five thousand), and in default thereof, to pay a fine as has been mentioned in the judgment.
He further submitted that the Petitioner is in custody for about two years.
The present I.A. has been filed with a prayer for release of the Petitioner on interim bail so that he can avail better treatment for his mother, who is ailing.

5. Learned counsel for the State, on instruction vide letter dated 03.12.2025 of the IIC, Simulia P.S.,
stated before this Court that on inquiry by the local police it was ascertained that the mother of the Bharat @ Sushanta Kumar vs State Of Odisha on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78000797/

sentences.text: Petitioner is suffering from hyper tension and is taking medicine regularly.
However, no details of the specific treatment have been produced before the police.
The IIC has stated in his report that the condition of the mother of the Petitioner is well.

As a reply to the same, learned counsel for the Appellant contended that although the health condition of the mother of the Petitioner is grave,
however he is not in a position to produce any medical documents.

6. Taking into consideration the fact that the Petitioner has already been convicted and he is languishing in custody for two years, and that there is no possibility of the appeal being heard in the near future, the Petitioner is allowed to go on interim bail.

7. In view of the aforesaid position, this Court is inclined to release the Petitioner/Appellant on interim bail for a period of three weeks, subject to the Petitioner/Appellant furnishing a bail bond of Rs.40,000/- (rupees forty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court.
It is open to the learned trial Court to impose any other condition for release of the Petitioner on bail.
The aforesaid interim bail period shall be counted from the date of his release from custody.
8. It is further made clear that on expiry of interim bail period, the Appellant/Petitioner shall surrender before the court below positively and produce the surrender certificate by the next date.
9. The I.A. is disposed of accordingly.
10. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application in course of the day.

11. Heard.
12.
Admit.

13. Call for the digitized copy of the TCR.
14.
As per the report of the IIC, Simulia P.S. notice of the appeal memo has already been served on the father of victim/informant on 17.11.2025.
15. However, none appears on behalf of the informant when the matter was called.
16. List this appeal on 12th January, 2026.
Surrender certificate be filed by the next date positively.
